title: Exploration of Field-Guided Assemblies of Magnetic Nanoparticles into Superstructures
summary: In this emerging line we aim at developing template-free strategies to engineer magnetic nanoparticle superstructures whose assembly is directed by tunable dipolar interactions. By controlling particle size, shape, and surface chemistry, we create dynamic architectures that reversibly reorganize under external magnetic fields. These field-directed superstructures hold promise for microrobotics, targeted biomedical transport, and remotely controlled soft devices.
descriptionHtml:
Magnetic nanoparticles are ideal building blocks for creating dynamic and stimuli-responsive superstructures, thanks to their ability to interact and self-organize under applied magnetic fields. By finely adjusting their dipolar interactions through particle size, morphology, and surface chemistry, it is possible to drive the formation of assemblies and other controlled architectures. We design template-free strategies for generating magnetic superstructures and exploit the reversible and controllable nature of dipolar coupling to assemble structures that can respond, rearrange, and adapt to external magnetic cues. Such field-directed superstructures pave the way for next-generation applications in microrobotics, biomedical transport systems, and remotely controlled soft devices, where their programmable and reversible assembly is crucial for functional operation.

Relevant publications:
Pérez-Garrido, R.; Landi, C.; Cuenca-Juberías, J. M.; Tajuelo, J.; Valeriani, C.; Gavilán, H. and Martínez-Pedrero, F. (Preliminary findings – manuscript in preparation)
